conventions.convention: Angles are read modulo 2π in every coordinate; Fourier modes are exp(ik·ϑ), with k an integer vector and |k|₁ the sum of coordinate absolute values.
Complex action and parameter distances use maximum norms. B_r is the action polydisc, S_s is the angular strip, and O_h(Ω) is the open distance-h neighborhood of Ω. Empty-domain suprema are zero.
The symplectic form is Σ dϑ_i ∧ dI_i. In action-first order X_H = (−H_ϑ,H_I), and {f,g} = f_ϑ·g_I − f_I·g_ϑ; consequently {F,ν·I} = ν·F_ϑ.
Diophantine labels satisfy |k·ν| ≥ α|k|₁^(−τ) for every nonzero integer vector k, with α > 0 and τ > n−1. The label set can have empty interior or be empty.

General homological data are families over real labels; their norms are explicit suprema over those labels. Joint complex-parameter data are Fourier-truncated, and h ≤ α/(2K^(τ+1)) preserves the retained divisors with constant α/2.
The iteration starts at j = 0, uses μ = τ+3n+2, angular loss 8σ_j, σ_j = σ₀2^(−j), K_j = K₀4^j, h_j = h₀4^(−μj), and E_(j+1) = C_*E_j^(3/2).
Frequency retractions are part of the extended compositions. The limiting torus has target rotation frequency ν for the original Hamiltonian evaluated at parameter χ∞(ν).

Positive-measure assertions use Lebesgue measure under Countable Choice. They make no probability or empirical frequency claim. The rotor coupling must be bounded in the complex strip norm, giving the factor cosh(s₀)².

load_bearing.statement: Under its stated domain, cutoff, reality and smallness hypotheses, with E = ε/(αrσ^μ) ≤ cη and μ = τ+3n+2, the affine zero-mean generator has a holomorphic canonical time-one flow; (N+P)∘Φ = N+R̂+P₊, and |P₊|_(ηr,s−8σ,h) ≤ C[E+η²+σ^(−n)exp(−σK/2)]ε. Its mean frequency shift satisfies |v| ≤ Cε/r.

Under initial conditions 1–3 of its Statement, every j ≥ 0 satisfies clauses (a)–(g), and ε_(j+1) = C_*2^(−μ)E_jε_j ≥ 3CE_jε_j. Thus the one-step remainder budget closes after frequency retraction. For 0 < α ≤ 1 the allowed initial E₀ threshold can be chosen independently of α.

Under the sequence hypotheses and specified one-step data, the extended compositions (Ψ_j,χ_j) converge on {0}×S_(s₀/4)×Λ, with uniform convergence of every angular derivative, the stated size and frequency-Lipschitz bounds, and the exact finite-stage identity H₀(Ψ_j(z,ν),χ_j(ν)) = e_j(ν)+ν·I+P_j(z,ν).

For the bounded periodic holomorphic data of its two stated types, Fourier coefficients have exponential decay, Fourier series equal the function on smaller strips and admit local termwise differentiation, coordinate derivatives obey the stated Cauchy bounds, lattice shells satisfy # {|k|₁=m} ≤ 4^n m^(n−1), and the stated exponential lattice-sum and cutoff bounds hold.

Under the composed-map hypotheses and additional CE₀ ≤ 1/16, every Diophantine label satisfies X_H(Ψ∞(0,ϑ,ν);χ∞(ν)) = Σν_j∂_(ϑ_j)Ψ∞(0,ϑ,ν); the parametrized rotation is an integral curve, and the pullback of the symplectic form vanishes.

Assuming Countable Choice and analytic data 1–4 of its Statement, there is c > 0 depending only on the fixed analytic data, n, τ, s₀ and σ₀ such that every 0 < α < c and 0 < ε ≤ cα² yield positive-measure Diophantine labels, embedded real invariant Lagrangian tori, the stated closeness and label-Lipschitz bounds, and a union of positive 2n-dimensional phase-space Lebesgue measure.

concerns.concern: The norm paragraph writes |g|_(r,s) := |g|_(r,s,0) := sup over B_r×S_s, while the general definition gives |g|_(r,s,h) as the supremum over B_r×S_s×O_h(Ω). Since O_0(Ω) is empty under the stated strict-distance definition, these prescriptions disagree at h = 0. The later homological lemma explicitly avoids this problem with its real-label supremum, so this is a notation clarification rather than a demonstrated failure of the iteration.

Proof step 3.1 says that 'the flow composition law transfers their C1 dependence to the entire trajectory', but lem-cm-local-flow-composition-law is absent from deps and the Facts citations. I opened that supplier: its composition and inverse-time laws have the needed domain-qualified statements. The local argument is sound once this actual prerequisite is identified.

Proof step 1.2 writes Ψ_j = Φ_0∘⋯∘Φ_(j−1) and x_i = Φ_i(x_(i+1)) without defining these Φ_i or carrying the retracted parameter coordinate. The supplier defines extended maps T_i and (Ψ_j,χ_j); the phase Jacobian product is valid when evaluated along those extended compositions. The current shorthand obscures this essential parameter bookkeeping, although the Statement and steps 1.1 and 3.1 retain χ_j correctly.

The page summarizes the parameter theorem as 'X_H∘Ψ∞ = DΨ∞·(0,ν)' without recording the original parameter χ∞(ν). The cited theorem explicitly establishes invariance for H(·;χ∞(ν)), not generally H(·;ν). The page should retain that qualification when describing the parameter-family result.
